ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the points $A(-6, 2)$ and $B(n, -4)$ are two intersection points of the linear function $y=kx+b$ and the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{m}{x}$. Find the expressions for the inverse proportion function and the linear function.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Substitute $A(-6, 2)$ into $y=\frac{m}{x}$, thus we get $m=2\times(-6)=-12$, \\
$\therefore$ the inverse proportion function equation is $y=-\frac{12}{x}$, \\
Substituting $B(n, -4)$ into $y=-\frac{12}{x}$, it yields $-4=-\frac{12}{n}$, \\
Solving that gives $n=3$, \\
Substituting $A(-6, 2)$ and $B(3, -4)$ into $y=kx+b$, we get \\
$\begin{cases}
-6k+b=2\\ 
3k+b=-4
\end{cases}$, resulting in: $\begin{cases}
k=-\frac{2}{3}\\ 
b=-2
\end{cases}$, \\
$\therefore$ the linear function equation is $\boxed{y=-\frac{2}{3}x-2}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, the horizontal axis is the x-axis, the vertical axis is the y-axis, and the origin is marked as O. A straight line slanting downward to the right intersects an inverse proportional function curve at two points: the upper-left intersection point is marked as A, and the lower-right intersection point is marked as B; the figure also marks C near the x-axis. The problem text gives that A(-6,2), B(n,-4) are the two intersection points of the straight line y=kx+b and the inverse proportional function y=m/x. Reasoning: Because A(-6,2) is on the inverse proportional function y=m/x, m=x\cdot y=(-6)\times 2=-12. Therefore the inverse proportional function is y=-12/x. Also because B(n,-4) is also on y=-12/x, substituting gives -4=-12/n, solving gives n=3. Therefore the coordinates of B are (3,-4). Next use A(-6,2) and B(3,-4) to find the slope of the straight line: k=(-4-2)/(3-(-6))=-6/9=-2/3. Substitute B(3,-4) into y=kx+b, obtaining -4=(-2/3)\cdot 3+b=-2+b, so b=-2. Therefore the linear function is y=-2x/3-2.
